title: Reconcile partial request payloads and session quotas for mid-stream disconnects
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: When clients open streaming sessions and submit multipart/partial input (for example: typed prompt fragments, file-chunk uploads, or client-side autosave sends), we currently either: 1) optimistically reserve quota up-front using the declared length, leading to overcharges when clients abort; or 2) bill only after finalization, which causes under-reservation and transient quota denial for long-running sessions. Mid-stream disconnects (network drop, client crash, or tab close) create ambiguous accounting: which input tokens were consumed, which outputs should be billed, and how to align that with quota enforcement windows and rate limiter buckets. This ticket defines a reconciliation design and implementation plan to make usage metering deterministic and correct for partial/mid-stream payloads while keeping user-visible latency low.
acceptance_criteria: Accounting invariant: for every session ID and finalization outcome (complete/aborted/timeout), the sum of billed input+output tokens equals the audited canonical token consumption computed from stored event stream
Quota enforcement preserves user experience: long-lived sessions should not be unfairly throttled due to optimistic reservations more than 500ms of additional startup latency
Reconciliation job reduces overcharged events to <0.01% of monthly usage and emits corrective adjustments visible in billing logs and dashboards
All events involved in reconciliation are traceable and surface a correlation_id/session_id in the Console and debug traces
New metrics (reconciliation_corrections, reservation_release_lag, partial_input_fraction) land in Grafana and alert when thresholds exceed expected bounds
technical_notes: Introduce a two-tier reservation model: lightweight soft reservations at session start based on declared or heuristic input length; then incremental hard-commit on chunk-confirmation or first model-token-emission

Persist every partial-input/stream-chunk event to the append-only metering topic (Kafka) with sequence numbers and finalization flags; this single source-of-truth is used by both realtime quota decisions and offline reconciliation
Rate limiter integration: soft reservations decrement a 'soft_quota' counter (non-blocking, can be reclaimed). Hard-commit decrements official quota counters that are used for enforcement

Idle/aborted session handling: if session closed without finalization, mark as ABORTED and run a deterministic scan to compute billable tokens from stored chunks + model consumption logs; release leftover soft reservations immediately

Reconciliation worker: idempotent batch processor (per session window) that compares committed counts vs provisional reservations and emits adjustment records (credit or debit). Adjustments flow to billing ledger as corrective ledger entries
Careful ordering guarantees are required: include monotonic sequence numbers and enforce causal reads when reconciling across metering topic partitions
Backwards compatibility: for sessions older than reconciliation rollout time, reconciliation job will run in a compatibility mode that is conservative (emit credit-only corrections)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement soft/hard reservation signals and event persistence; enable on internal canary accounts for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (limited beta): enable reconciliation worker for 10% of production traffic; monitor reconciliation corrections and quota errors closely
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): expand to 50% then 100% with 24/7 monitoring and auto-rollback on high correction rate (>0.05% of total tokens) or user-reported billing regressions
Communication: PM to send customer advisory for enterprise customers about expected minor credit adjustments during first 2 billing cycles
tests: Unit tests for reservation state machine (soft->hard->release) with simulated disconnects
Integration tests that replay real-world session traces (typed prompts, multi-file uploads, network flaps) and assert final ledger matches reconciliation output
Chaos tests: simulate broker partition and consumer restart during reconciliation to verify idempotence and exactly-once semantics of adjustment records
Performance tests to ensure soft reservation path adds <5% tail latency to session setup and does not increase 95th percentile token latency by >10ms
references: Prior ticket: ENG-127501 (tokenization-drift-healing) - for tokenizer normalization approach
